body:
Review pass 38. RETRACTION - my Epic 8 scope recommendation was wrong, and your own profiling found the reason.

THE GATE RESULT (52416 features, support median 33):
  analysis_seconds     3476.43  (57.9 min)   runtime_pass FALSE
  plan_seconds           57.81
  crossnobis_seconds   3417.17  (98.3% of total)
  incremental peak RSS 2.05 GiB              memory_pass TRUE
  factorization_units  1.653e9
  structure_pass TRUE, exact NeuroVol mapping TRUE, passed FALSE

My predictions that runtime would fail and memory would not were right. My explanation was wrong, and that is what mattered.

I attributed the cost to per-support k-by-k solves and built a ceiling - "dense metrics unsupported above ~33000 nodes" - on the premise it was irreducible. The summary refutes that directly: 1.653e9 factorization units over 3417 s is 4.84e5 units/second. At a conservative 1e8 units/s the entire factorization workload is 16.5 s, 0.48% of measured; at 1e9 it is 1.7 s. This path was never solve-bound.

Worse, I had that number from pass 3 when I reviewed .support_index_cost and its dense_factorization_units field. I never sanity-checked it against measured runtime and reasoned from an assumed cost model instead of a profile.

YOUR DIAGNOSIS IS RIGHT AND IT IS MY OWN ORIGINAL FINDING COMING BACK: "59% of execution in repeated whole-frame/support validation." That is the validation-overhead problem from my first review - 779 stop() calls, .validate_relation on every block read, ~1344 validate calls and 371 SHA-256 digests per geometry() call, scaling with feature blocks. I filed it as an efficiency concern and then failed to connect it to a brain-scale runtime failure.

If your 7.1x speedup (28.091 s -> 3.971 s at 4096 features) carries to 52416: 3417/7.1 + 57.8 = 539 s = 9.0 minutes against a 30-minute gate. Dense local metrics would PASS at full brain scale, and the scope split would be exactly the wrong thing to certify.

So: do not adopt the scope split. The rerun you have already launched is the right next step and I will verify it rather than project.

Still standing, unaffected: the fixture is statistically degenerate - 84% of supports have k > residual df - so once runtime is settled, re-run at a meaningful fixture before certifying.
